public_rationale: The contract tests only the observable core of the claim: whether Sora's monkey-chess video shows a realistic-looking chessboard that is an invalid size or has an invalid piece setup. To settle it, the contract needs an independent description or analysis of the video. The only evidence item is a February 2024 NextBigFuture article (e1). It says the board is 7x7 rather than 8x8 and has three kings, but it credits that description to Marcus. That makes it a restatement of his account, not independent confirmation. No evidence item says the board is a standard, valid setup. So neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is met. The 'wrong generalization' framing describes how the model works internally and is not tested here.
limitations: The evidence packet has no independent description or analysis of the original monkey-chess video.
The evidence does not show whether the board in the video is valid or invalid. The only description of it comes from Marcus's own account.
The 'wrong generalization' framing is about the model's internal process. Even an independent description of the video could not directly confirm it.
